blocks.body: Sewer rodding clears a blocked main line with a long, flexible steel cable fed through a cleanout access point. A cutting head on the end breaks through roots, grease, and debris and pushes the blockage toward the street connection, restoring flow through the pipe. It's the standard first fix for a clogged or backed-up sewer line. For most homes, it's the only fix needed.

blocks.h2: Rodding Lines Under Elmhurst's Mid-Century Homes
blocks.body: About 4 in 10 Elmhurst homes went up between 1940 and 1969, and many still have their original clay laterals. Those pipes have short sections with a joint every few feet, and mature trees on established blocks have had decades to find them. A yearly rodding keeps roots from closing the line. If roots come back within months, the camera shows whether jetting or a liner would be a better use of your money.

blocks.h2: Sewer Rodding Questions From Elmhurst Homeowners

items.q: How often should an older Elmhurst home be rodded?
items.preview: Yearly if roots are a known problem.
items.answer: If roots have blocked your line before, once a year is common, usually in late winter.

items.q: Is rodding or jetting better for roots?
items.preview: Jetting lasts longer. Rodding is faster and simpler.
items.answer: Rodding cuts a path through the roots and works well for routine maintenance. [Hydro jetting](/elmhurst/hydro-jetting) removes more of the growth, so it usually lasts longer.

items.q: Can rodding damage old clay pipe?
items.answer: Not with the right cutter. The camera afterward shows whether the pipe was already cracked.

items.q: Where's the cleanout in an Elmhurst home?
items.preview: Usually in the basement near the floor drain.
items.answer: Usually in the basement near where the line leaves the house. Some homes also have one outside.

items.q: Should I be home during the rodding?
items.preview: Yes, to show us the cleanout.
items.answer: It helps, so you can show us the cleanout and see the footage.

items.q: How much does sewer rodding cost in Elmhurst?
items.preview: It depends on access and the clog. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the cleanout location, the length of the line and what's blocking it. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
